_comment: Config for the markdown-link-check CI gate (docs link-checker, #135). Scope is root *.md + docs/**. External http(s) URLs ARE checked: the repository has been public since 2026-07-22 (#697), so canonical github.com/nightgauge/* URLs resolve to an unauthenticated checker like any other public repo. Image assets are skipped: this gate validates cross-document reference integrity, not binary asset presence, and some operator-runbook screenshots are committed in follow-up PRs (see docs/images/*/README.md). Pure in-page #anchors are not resolved as files. aliveStatusCodes covers common bot-walling on third-party doc sites (401/403/429 from a WAF or rate limiter, 307 from a Next.js prefetch redirect with no Location header) -- a live site answering oddly to a headless checker is not a dead link. ERRORED requests are NOT handled here and deliberately so (#1004): `Status: 0` is this checker's marker for no HTTP response at all (DNS failure, timeout, TLS reset, connection refused, a bot filter dropping the runner), and adding 0 to aliveStatusCodes would also accept NXDOMAIN -- exactly the class the docs.openai.com/codex ignore entry below documents as genuinely dead. No config option separates the two, so scripts/check-md-links.sh re-probes every Status: 0 URL with curl and classifies it dead / unreachable-from-runner / alive-after-reprobe. The reasoning is in that script's header; its regression suite is scripts/test-check-md-links.sh.

ignorePatterns.comment: CHANGELOG.md compare links for a release section. The contract (docs/GIT_WORKFLOW.md § Changelog) lands the rollover PR BEFORE the tag is pushed, so at PR time the newest section's compare URLs 404 by construction -- the tag does not exist yet. scripts/check-changelog.sh guarantees every released tag has its section, and the tag's existence makes the links resolve; nothing else about the URL can be wrong, since the version segment is the same string the gate checks. Scoped to this repo's own compare URLs only.

Confirmed NXDOMAIN (#697 re-enablement sweep, 2026-08-18) -- docs.openai.com does not resolve at all. Genuinely dead; the doc should point at platform.openai.com/docs/codex or similar. Content fix is a separate, out-of-scope change; this ignore is deliberately URL-scoped, not a blanket exclusion.
